candidates.mechanism: A shared scheduled table writes one ordinary cover word for each payload character. The character selects a row; the current schedule position selects a column. The reader uses that same column to recover the character and advances according to the written rule.
candidates.human_purpose: Conceal a meaningful letter message inside a superficially grammatical cover text. Cover-word meanings are not payload-word meanings. This is different from assigning each whole source word a fixed address or shortening a source spelling.

candidates.paid_cost_if_completed: Every table entry, exact schedule, source alphabet, payload-space/punctuation convention, finite-book wrap/reset and decoding collision rule are needed. An unfamiliar source word could be spelled character by character only after those ordinary character/space rules are supplied. candidates.known_forms_by_hand: An exact whole-word triple requires that the same cover spelling be permitted in three successive schedule positions. It need not encode the same payload letter in all three. Different triple types require their own memberships in that same frozen table. A two-sign whole group requires a cover word of that actual encoded length; a long word with varied interiors needs a corresponding whole cover spelling. No such memberships, lengths or graphical mappings are established by the card, so no shape match is claimed.

candidates.human_purpose: A mnemonic cue for previously known formulae or passages. Writing the initials is easy; reconstructing arbitrary previously unknown ordinary clauses is not an inverse supplied by this projection.

Every whole word remains counted, and the clauses have the same structure and number of words. Any one global injective recoding of their initials gives the same written group. candidates.known_forms_by_hand: Two-sign and long groups can formally represent two-word and many-word clauses. Repeated whole codes can represent repeated clauses or different clauses with identical initials; a native triple therefore is not itself a contradiction. Conversely, formal ol/olol or daldy-family capacity does not select any underlying clause, repeated action, plural or morpheme. Group length merely counts source words under the declared projection.

Its missing owned target hierarchy and fixed clipping rule remain; a mnemonic source does not silently provide123's complete clause dictionary.
candidates.paid_cost_if_completed: Either preserve a declared ambiguous set of clauses as the whole information contract, or provide a fixed learned repertoire with enough written disambiguation to distinguish its preimages. The latter information has a real vocabulary/control cost. Neither an arbitrary new clause list nor an unspoken author's intended sentence is free. Ordinary clause boundaries, punctuation and unknown-name spelling still need a complete channel.
candidates.decision: No open-message hand writer nominated. Another initials roundtrip would demonstrate only the projection. A particular fixed-repertoire test could have a different question, but no new repertoire, native key or source selection is proposed here.

candidates.mechanism: Write each consonant as a fixed baseline body and stack every immediately following vowel above that same body in source order. An initial vowel run uses a distinct empty carrier K. Keep complete source-word spaces.
candidates.human_purpose: Preserve all spelling letters while displaying consonant bodies and their vowel runs in separate spatial positions. This is a hand-executable spatial alphabet schema, not a cover-word table or mnemonic omission rule.
candidates.state: Curated inconclusive with a concrete failed conditional carrier binding. It is not wholly unexamined. Its teaching inventory explicitly costs21consonant bodies, five vowel marks and K, a27-drawing reference table. A complete physical22-working-sign realization is not supplied. The number27is a teaching-table cost, not a new proof about native atoms or a license to merge body and mark types.
candidates.known_forms_by_hand: A one-consonant word is one bare body; an initial vowel requires K plus its mark. Repeating any complete word, including three times, repeats the same construction without a universal repeat header. Long words can contain many body types, so no fixed three-interior-type cap follows. Word-final vowels remain marks above the last body, not automatically a recurring linear suffix. These are abstract writing properties, not assignments of native ol, dy, e, i or any gallows.
candidates.strongest_retained_countercase: In the exact already tested G1/body-cap projection, ch is bare in chor and medial/bare in qopchey, so it cannot be K, which must be initial and bear a nonempty stack. No observed body met all K obligations. This did not refute an unobserved K or prove native consonant/vowel identities. SOURCE865's tau/mu additions do not attest the proposed complete all-vowel system.
candidates.full_message_limit: The current A-Z teaching domain excludes punctuation and other characters instead of supplying their physical spelling. Whole words are moved intact between rows; no finite-width handling exists for an arbitrarily overwide word or arbitrarily tall vowel run. A source-independent proof of reversibility over cells does not pay these physical limitations.
candidates.decision: Do not repeat the same cap/empty-carrier audit or another alphabet lesson. A genuinely different justified spatial/body binding or a separately declared complete physical writer would be needed; neither is created here.
